posts.author: DJ Mathson
posts.content_md: I saw those "waveplates" also and contacted the seller about it and told him that I thought it was polarizers he was selling. He replied but did not change the description.

posts.author: wler
posts.content_md:
> **DJ Mathson:** I saw those "waveplates" also and contacted the seller about it and told him that I thought it was polarizers he was selling. He replied but did not change the description.

Yes they seem to be some sort of polarizers; when two are tilted 90 degrees with respect to each other, then there is a dip in intensity but by far not as much as for "good" polarizers - I estimate perhaps 10% of light ist still getting through. So I am not sure what these things really are - perhaps made for a specific wavelength. (BTW the guy charges $19 for a shipment to Europe, the weight of which was less than 10 grams and would easily have fit into an ordinary letter envelope. )

posts.author: edelbrp
posts.content_md:
BTW- The market price for used Coherent 315M-100's might finally be going down. I noticed this one went for $650:

[http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?Vi ... 34556&rd=1](http://cgi.ebay.com/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&category=7321&item=3844234556&rd=1)

I thought I also saw just the laser head (no power supply) go for $300, but I couldn't find that auction again.

Is a Coherent 315M-100 really the most cost effective way to get into DCG? I'd love to try DCG, but finding an affordable laser seems pretty tough. There are other *really* cheap ones, but operation is intended to be itermittent (pointer) and/or have a coherence length in the mm's.

-Phil
